implementation_notes: The cleanest Ruby Table Module is a Sequel dataset: DB[:orders] is the table-level object, dataset methods (where, select, order, group, update, delete) are the set-oriented operations, and they are chainable and frozen, so the module stays stateless and thread-safe; execution methods such as .all return an array of hashes, which is the record set. Rules live in methods that take a dataset and return another dataset, or a result array. ActiveRecord is a different pattern - a per-row model instance with its own lifecycle is Active Record/Domain Model, not a table module - so do not present an AR model as one.
pitfalls: Sequel datasets are lazy: a chain that never ends in an execution method (all/each/update/delete) silently performs no work, and calling .all first and then filtering in Ruby pulls the whole table into memory.

Datasets are bound to a connection pool: a dataset built from a global DB constant raises only at execution time if the pool is closed, and per-request state smuggled into the constant leaks between requests.
